title: Volume 1 Chapter 5: Skill Certification 1
content: Sayori and Karla. The nails for their shoot were complete.
I had painted their toenails the same as the "starry sky design" I had done on their hands. Sayori was wearing a swimsuit under her uniform, but I wasn’t flustered this time.
We had arrived at a photo studio in the city.
Surprisingly, this studio had a pool inside the building. I felt like I had seen a background like this in special effects or dramas before.
It reminded me that both Sayori and Karla were working as models.
"Okay, you two, look this way!"
"Yay!" "Peace!"
"So cute!"
As the photographer called out, the two of them posed happily for the camera.

The shutter clicks had been going off dozens of times, but only a small portion would actually be used in the magazine. Still, it was clear that every staff member was serious about each shot they took.
Of course, Sayori and Karla, who were being photographed, were just as serious.
"Sayori-chan, that nail is lovely! Let’s get a close-up!"
The photographer, speaking in a feminine tone, said that.
"Right? You can tell, can’t you? Of course! Take lots of photos!"
"Okay, here we go, give me your best smile☆"
Sayori showcased her nails to the camera, looking pleased at the compliment.
(...I’m glad for her.)
Now, as for me, who had come to this unfamiliar setting.
While the professional staff busily moved around, I sat in a corner, trying to make myself small. I had brought a plastic toolbox.
Inside were all the tools I needed for nail art. While I couldn’t redo the nails from scratch, I was prepared for repairs and adjustments.
Well, I thought I wouldn’t need to fix nails on set unless something major happened.
(Was it really necessary for me to come along?)
Sayori had insisted, so I had accompanied her to the studio, but to be honest, I felt like I had no role here.
I felt like the staff were looking at me with expressions that said, "Who’s this wallflower?"—and it was unbearable.
No, that was just paranoia. I had been introduced by Sayori and had greeted everyone.
At the shoot, there were not only the photographer but also lighting staff, makeup artists, and Karla’s agency manager.
I was technically there as a nail artist, but there was no way someone like me could claim that title next to professional makeup artists.
For a moment, I even considered sneaking away, which was a bad habit of mine as a socially awkward introvert.
"Hello."
As I was lost in those escape thoughts.
A woman with a refreshing smile sat across from me.
"How’s it going, Azuma-kun? You seem uncomfortable at the shoot."
"Well, it’s not great—just not familiar with it."
"Ahaha! I get that!"
Even when I said something negative, she laughed it off.
With a somewhat androgynous face, she could easily pass for a male model—but she was apparently an editor from the fashion magazine where Sayori and the others would be featured.
She was the only one in a suit at this shoot.
From her head sprouted small horns, and bat-like wings extended from her back. She was also a demi-human.
"Did Sayori-chan tell you about me?"
"Um… just your name. It was Mio-chan, right?"
"That’s fine. Just call me that!"
Mio-chan winked at me, but honestly, I didn’t have any information about her other than her name.
Watching Sayori talk to Mio-chan over the phone, I thought being an editor must be tough.
"Sayori-chan talks about you all the time. It’s amazing that you can do nails for a dragon demi-human with your plastic model skills!"
"Well, it was just a coincidence."
I had a similar conversation with Karla.
How much was Sayori spreading the word about me? She didn’t even tell her friends at school that I was doing nails.
"Do you study nail art on your own?"
"Yeah, I guess… I just look things up online and learn by imitation. Sayori has taught me a lot too, but there’s still so much I don’t know."
"Is that so? Sayori-chan and Karla-chan’s nails were painted beautifully! There were no streaks, and the finish was excellent. If you studied properly, you could open a nail salon in no time."
"You’re overpraising me."
"No, no, I’m an editor for a fashion magazine, so I have a discerning eye! There aren’t many nails that can bring out a model’s charm like that!"
Mio-chan was really enthusiastic.
Maybe because she was from the glamorous world of fashion, she had no hesitation in communicating. She was just like Sayori in that regard.
"Sayori-chan is great! She has charisma and takes amazing photos! Plus, there aren’t many demi-human models, so I wish she would officially join an agency like Karla-chan."
"Does that mean you’re not considered a pro unless you’re with an agency?"

"Well, there are freelance models, so it’s not that simple. Right now, Sayori-chan is in the reader model category, so she’s still an amateur… But since she’s popular and easy to contact, I’m asking you to be her pinch hitter like this."
I glanced at Sayori.
Lying on a beach chair and striking a pose, Sayori waved at me when she noticed my gaze, showing the back of her hand.
That was probably a nail showcase.
"Sayori-chan wants to enjoy her student life, so she doesn’t seem to have any intention of becoming a professional model."
"I see."
"But she’s been struggling with not being able to get her nails done for a long time, so having someone like you who can help her is really a relief for me."
"Um, how should I put it…?"
Was she trying to put pressure on me?
To keep helping Sayori with her nails?
"Oh, I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to put pressure on you."
"Well, I definitely felt pressure just now…?"
I unconsciously distanced myself emotionally.

"demi-human models are still quite rare. Just like Karla-chan, having a model with the charm of someone like Sayori-chan can inspire young demi-humans and broaden the fashion options for demi-humans."
It seemed that Mio-chan really valued Sayori.
I remembered how there were so few swimsuits for demi-humans in the swimwear section. For girls who wanted to try on different styles like Sayori, it could be a matter of life and death.
"As an editor for a fashion magazine, I want to cherish models like Sayori-chan. I believe that her enjoying the shoot will lead to the magazine’s quality."
"Is that how it works?"
"Nail art is definitely necessary for that."
I fell silent.
Could someone like me, still in the learning phase, really do something so grand?
All I was doing was painting nails.
Mio-chan would probably say that was enough.
Sayori might say that too. But still, I was still—
"Fufu♪"
As I was lost in thought, Mio-chan began to smile mischievously.
This kind of smile was so similar to Sayori’s. Usually, after this, I’d be asked for something, so I instinctively became wary.
"W-what is it?"
"Because right now, you looked like you were wondering what you could do for Sayori-chan, right? Fufu, you know, I love seeing young people with ambition! You’re making me emotional!"
"Ugh…"
I wasn’t good at the teasing that older people often did.
"I’d like to introduce you to something."
"Uh? What is this—"
Mio-chan pulled out a thin booklet. It was titled "Nailist Skill Certification Examination Guidelines."
"Skill certification…?"
"Exactly! Do you know about nailist qualifications?"
"No, not at all. I didn’t even know there were qualifications."
"Fufu, I thought so. Just buying polish and applying it is something even a cheeky elementary school student could do. Just applying it—"
Mio-chan rested her chin on her hand with a smug expression.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/3bgfeqy.jpeg
"However, if you want to earn money as a professional nailist or open a nail salon, you'll need qualifications, right?"
"National qualifications... what are those?"

"No, it's run by a private organization—right here." Mio-chan pointed to the corner of the booklet. The name of the certifying organization was written there. "Several organizations conduct nail-related certification exams, but one of the most famous is the Japan Nailist Certification Examination Center, often abbreviated as JNEC. There are levels from first to third grade for the nailist certification."
"Wow, that's quite a serious qualification... it sounds difficult."

"Haha, there's practical work involved, and depending on how you look at it, it might be tougher than school exams? To take the certification, you need to bring a model who will receive the nail treatment. Well, in your case, you might not lack for volunteers—" Mio-chan glanced at Sayori, who was being photographed. "However, this qualification, if you're taking the third grade exam, it's said that you can pass it through self-study... It's written in the guidelines too, but as long as you've graduated from compulsory education—middle school—you can take the third grade exam, so if you're interested, I hope you'll consider it."
"Uh-huh."
"I think the teaching materials for this certification are sold in the qualification exam section of bookstores."
As for my interest—honestly, I had some.
In plastic model making, there are no qualifications or certifications. Basically, anyone can learn on their own.
On the other hand, nail art has qualifications to obtain objective evaluations. If I could study properly and apply that knowledge to Sayori's nails, it didn't seem like a bad idea.
After all, since she's a reader model, it would be better for her to have her nails done by someone whose skills are widely recognized. Qualifications could serve as a good indicator.
"Oh, and don't get me wrong, this isn't mandatory or anything."

"Of course, if you get qualified, I think you'll be able to make Sayori-chan shine even more. But studying costs money, and the exam fees aren't cheap. I'm just recommending it; I just wanted to let you know that such qualifications exist." Mio-chan winked at me.
Is this person really not a model? Every gesture she makes is so graceful. She gives off the impression of a woman who is popular with other women.
"By the way, there’s also something called a gel nail certification. If you can do both, it will further expand your range of expression."
"Ah, um—thank you."
I hurriedly bowed my head.
It seemed she had only come to introduce me to the certification.
"No, no, if you really become Sayori-chan's nailist, I would be happy too—there might come a day when I can ask you for work, you know?"
"No way—"
That would be too much of an overestimation.
"Don't underestimate the eyes of an editor. I'm looking forward to it."
"Ha, haha..."
Could it be that this was a comment made with expectations for my future growth?
Becoming a nailist.
I had never thought about my future like that, but looking at the certification guidelines in front of me, suddenly that option felt more realistic.
(No, no)
For now, I was just doing nails as an extension of my hobbies and friendships.
I still had no idea how things would turn out. I needed to think it over carefully.
"Azuma-kun, I'm sorry!"
While I was lost in thought, Sayori, in her swimsuit, came running toward me.
I had been so focused on the qualifications that I hadn't looked at Sayori.
As she ran along the poolside, I couldn't help but notice her chest and tail swaying. I had seen them when I painted her pedicure, but seeing them again on set was quite stimulating.
"I bumped my foot! My pedicure might have come off!"
"Okay, okay, let me take a look..."
It shouldn't be that easy to come off, but where did she bump it?
Sayori sat on a chair by the poolside and stretched her legs out. I knelt down at her feet to check the area around her injured toe.
"Ah, here it is."
There was a small scratch on the top coat. It should be fine if I just repaint over it.
I took out the top coat from the plastic case I had brought. The repair work was finished quickly.
"Don't move until it dries."
"Okay—oh, you were talking to Mio-chan, right? What were you talking about?"
"Ah, about nail qualifications and stuff."
"Oh, Mio-chan is super knowledgeable! She has a makeup qualification too, and she used to do makeup for models back in the day!"
"That person can do anything..."
When I glanced at Mio-chan, she was watching me with a smile as I knelt at Sayori's feet.
It felt like I could hear someone saying, "Ah, youth," but that was just my own assumption.
"I also learned a lot from Mio-chan..."
"Okay, okay, too close, too close."

Why does she always lean in so close when she talks? Because of that, the beauty made up by a professional is right in front of me, and her chest is also coming closer. Being at Sayori's feet makes the swaying of her chest even more distracting.
"Look, it's already dry. Go on."
"Okay! So, Azuma-kun, watch me!"
"Sure, I'll be watching."
Honestly, I had no idea where to look, but if I said I wasn't watching, Sayori would get upset.
Phew, I sighed as I glanced at the certification guidelines on the beach table.
(Qualifications, huh—)
I pondered for a moment.
In the end, I put the certification guidelines I received from Mio-chan into my bag.
(What should I do?)
I felt like I was moving according to Mio-chan's wishes. It was as if I was in the palm of an adult, but I didn't feel bad about it.
After all, I genuinely wanted to improve my nail skills.
After that, the photoshoot with Sayori and Karla proceeded smoothly. I couldn't help but think that I really didn't need to be there.
"Yay, I was amazing, right, Azuma-kun!"
"Yeah, you were amazing. As expected of a model."
"Right? Yay♪"
Seeing Sayori's excited expression made it all worth it.
Several days passed since the photoshoot at the pool.
After school, I stopped by a bookstore before heading to the garage to look for books on certification exams.
(Nailist certification... found it, this is it.)
I quickly located the teaching materials Mio-chan had mentioned.
I flipped through the pages. Starting with the guidelines for the nailist certification, it covered how to handle tools, the process of treatments, and basic knowledge of nails and hand care.
It also seemed to check whether you could create nail art according to the theme.
(...It looks like a serious exam.)
I wondered if I could really manage it through self-study.
The teaching materials were quite user-friendly, detailing the exam items with pictures.
(Well, it's only natural, but it's all for human nails.)
There was nothing about how to use a hand grinder.
I realized again that I had been painting Sayori's nails in a rather unconventional way. It was true that she had no other way to get her nails done.
The teaching materials included safety for nails, knowledge about diseases, and the mindset required when touching and handling other people's hands.
Nowhere did it say that it was okay to file nails with tools meant for models.
(I was applying things without knowing the basics...)
I thought I had been careful enough.
But if Sayori got hurt, it might not just be about nails anymore.
(...Should I buy it?)
I was still contemplating whether to take the exam.
However, I felt that the knowledge written in the certification materials was necessary for me right now.
After buying the book, I headed to the garage.
I sat at my usual work desk, flipping through the teaching materials while being careful not to overlook anything.
"Ah, Azuma-kun!"
Just as I read a few pages, a monster, or rather, a gal, burst in.
She opened the garage door with an intonation I had never heard before.
"Okay, okay, welcome."
I ended up responding like a ramen shop owner.
I set the teaching materials aside and looked at Sayori, who was sitting in front of me.
"Thanks for coming to the shoot! Mio-chan said you're amazing and could totally handle work!"
"T-thank you..."
Is it just that cheerful people are good at giving compliments? I wasn't used to being praised, so I didn't know how to respond.
"They told me to bring you along for the next shoot. So if you're okay with it, I’d like to go together—"
Sayori's eyes were fixed on the teaching materials I had left on the work desk.
"Is that the nailist certification stuff? Are you going to get qualified, Azuma-kun?!"
"Ah, no, I'm still thinking about it..."
"Is that so? You’ll definitely pass! I guarantee it!"
"That's why I said I'm still deciding whether to take it or not."
As usual, she was moving the conversation along rapidly.
"I learned about the certification from Mio-chan. Regardless of whether I take the exam or not, I thought I should at least know the basics."
"Uh-huh, Azuma-kun, you’ll remember it in no time! You're already a nailist!"
"That's a bit premature..."
"Ah!? Are you putting it away?!"
Sayori was so loud that I put the certification teaching materials away in the magazine rack where I kept my magazines.
"Well, for now, I'm planning to study, so don't worry too much about it. So, what are we doing today?"
"Um, Karla said she still wanted to keep this nail on, but I think I’ll take it off early."
"Is that okay?"
"Yeah! For me, it's just for the shoot!"
"Got it. Then let's take off your nails today and next time, we can paint a new color."
"Okay!"
Using the remover, I started to take off Sayori's nails.
I was already quite used to this part, but reading the certification materials might lead to new discoveries. Learning systematically is important.
I decided to read the teaching materials again for review.
"Hey, Azuma-kun."
Sayori asked while looking at her nails that I had just removed.
"Are you really going to become a nailist?"
"......I wonder."
I still didn't know what I wanted to do.
"But nail art is fun. It might be one of the paths for my future."
"Is that so?"
"It’s tough to make a living just from plastic models... If I had qualifications, it would feel like I had a skill, and I might have more options."
"Wow, you're really thinking about the future... that's so mature."
Sayori put her hands on her head in exasperation. What kind of reaction is that after asking me?
"So, what about you, Sayori? Are you going to become a model?"
"Eh? I don't know... Shooting with Karla and Mio-chan is fun, but... becoming a pro feels different..."
"Then what do you want to do?"
"Hmm... maybe a bride?"
"That's not something you write down on a career plan!"
"Boo."
It seemed that Sayori had no plan regarding her future.
Pouting her lips, she looked sulky.
Well, this kind of lighthearted conversation felt very student-like. Eventually, we would have to face these realities.
For now, it was fine to talk freely about the future.
"If I really open a nail salon, will you come?"
I said it jokingly, of course, I had no intention of doing so.
I just thought Sayori would nod as if it were a given.
"Ah... yeah, I’ll definitely go."
That's strange. Normally, Sayori would say something like, "Of course I will!" in an overly enthusiastic manner.
It seemed that the idea of me opening a salon felt strange to her. Well, I guess that's understandable. I wouldn't know what women would like.
It might be a reminder that an introvert should keep their dreams in check.
"No, the salon is just a joke. More importantly, think about what kind of nails you want next."
"Ah, okay! Thanks for today, Azuma-kun!"
Sayori began to get ready to leave.
I was still contemplating about qualifications and salons—after all, we were still students.
For now, it felt just right to slowly think about what polish to use next with Sayori in the garage.
I felt that being able to affirm the present was a good thing.
"See you, Azuma-kun! Until tomorrow!"
"Yeah, see you tomorrow."
Just that simple exchange confirmed that Sayori would come to the garage again tomorrow.
As students with no plans for the future, maybe it was best for us to only think about tomorrow, I thought.
I was thinking that when the "tomorrow" suddenly fell into crisis.
"Hajime. I need to talk to you."
"—Dad?"
As soon as I returned home from the garage, my father approached me with a furrowed brow.
I was not good with this expression of his. It usually meant I was about to get scolded.
"Is something wrong?"
My father wasn't the type to raise his voice and yell.
He would calmly point out my faults with logical reasoning, making it almost pointless to argue or make excuses. Even if I was in the wrong, I found it hard to deal with him during these times.
"Sit down."
No, he really seemed to be angry.
My father looked at me straight with a stern expression.
"Hajime. Today, I received a phone call at my workplace. When I answered, there was an inquiry asking if we do nails."
A foolish sound escaped my mouth.
An inquiry about nails—why would that be at my father's workplace?
"Of course, I told them that we are a car repair shop... but I could tell it wasn't just a wrong number. You understand, right?"
"Because I'm doing nails in the garage?"
"That's the only conclusion I can come to."
I was stunned.
Indeed, if there was an inquiry about nails at my father's workplace, the only connection would be that I was doing Sayori's nails in the garage.
